text:
Elliot Price: Hey folks — could use eyes on the updated Streaming Responses page before we merge. Goal is: consistent headings across Python/TS/Go, clear event semantics, and a couple warning callouts. PR here: https://github.com/redwood/redwood-docs/pull/901

Wei Chen: Looking now. Overall much better. A few notes as I read:
- Can we standardize the section headings to match Tools + Structured Outputs pages? e.g. `## Overview`, `## Event types`, `## Basic streaming loop`, `## Getting the final response`, `## Troubleshooting`.
- In `Event types`, we should explicitly say “delta events are partial” in the first paragraph. Right now it’s implied but easy to miss.

Elliot Price: Yep, agree. I mirrored what we had on the old page but can update to the new IA. Do you prefer `Event types` vs `Stream events`?

Wei Chen: `Stream events` reads better IMO, but whatever we pick should match the SDK guide phrasing. If the SDK docs say “event model”, I’d go `Stream events` + first sentence “The stream yields a sequence of events…”.

Sabrina James: +1 to making the headings match the other pages. Also: a couple of code blocks have extra blank lines that make copy/paste weird (esp the TS example with the abort controller). I can push a formatting cleanup commit if you want.

Elliot Price: Please do :pray: (or I can fold it in). I’m trying to avoid churn but formatting fixes are safe.

Kira Thompson: Read-through from ops angle: we should add a warning callout about proxy buffering. We keep seeing customers behind NGINX / corporate proxies where streaming “hangs” until the buffer flushes. Something like:
> If you’re behind a proxy/load balancer, ensure response buffering is disabled for SSE/streaming, and use a client that flushes output as it arrives.
We can keep it short but having it on the page will reduce support pings.

Wei Chen: Yes please. Also, minor wording:
- In the Python snippet, `print(event.delta, end="")` is fine, but add a comment “don’t assume deltas are complete sentences”.
- For “Getting the final response”: call out that usage/token counts are only available on the final event / final response object. People keep asking why `usage` is null mid-stream.

Ibrahim Khan: Jumping in — for event semantics, let’s be explicit:
- “delta” events may contain partial UTF-8 sequences depending on transport boundaries (rare, but can happen); best practice is append to a buffer and render as you like.
- The stream ends with a final “completed” event (or equivalent final response) that includes `id`, `usage`, and the fully assembled message.
If the docs can say “don’t treat any single event as authoritative; only the final response is complete”, that would align with the canonical patterns doc.

Elliot Price: Good call. I’ll add a short paragraph under Stream events + a warning callout. I want to avoid getting too deep into implementation details, but the “usage only in final” note is important.

Sabrina James: I’ll take the formatting pass + a small consistency tweak:
- In Go, we use `for stream.Next() { ... }` and in TS we say “iterate events”; maybe add the same label in each code block header: “Loop over events” so it visually lines up.

Wei Chen: Another small thing: the page currently has `### Reconnecting` as a subheader. We should be careful not to imply reconnect/resume is guaranteed. Maybe rename to `### Handling disconnects` and say “retry the request” vs “resume the stream”.

Kira Thompson: +1. If we mention retry, we should also mention timeouts: “set an explicit read timeout / deadline so you don’t hang forever if the connection half-opens.”

Ibrahim Khan: Agree on wording. “Resume” is overloaded. We can say “If the stream disconnects, you may need to re-issue the request; design your app so it can tolerate partial output.”

Elliot Price: Updating:
- Rename `Reconnecting` -> `Handling disconnects`
- Add warning callout: proxy buffering + timeouts
- Add “final response” note: usage + canonical output
- Normalize headings to match Tools/Structured pages

Wei Chen: On the callout styling: can we use the standard “Warning” admonition? The draft uses bold text inline in a couple spots.

Elliot Price: Yep, will convert to the admonition block. Thanks.

Sabrina James: Pushed a commit on the PR with code block whitespace fixes + consistent comments across language snippets. Also swapped a couple `stream` vs `responseStream` variable names so they’re consistent within each snippet (not across languages, but at least not confusing).

Elliot Price: Saw it, looks good. :thumbsup: (reaction)

Wei Chen: Final editorial nit: in the intro, we say “streaming tokens”. Maybe say “streaming output deltas” instead, since not all events are one token and some SDKs chunk differently.

Ibrahim Khan: +1. “Token” implies 1:1 and that’s what trips people up.

Elliot Price: Done. Replaced with “output deltas” and added one sentence: “Chunking is transport- and SDK-dependent; treat deltas as incremental text.”

Kira Thompson: Looks good to me after those tweaks.

Wei Chen: Same. Approving once CI is green.

Elliot Price: Thanks all — merging after CI + I’ll carry these same headings into the troubleshooting page so they match.
